_readme: The cloud -> robot ACTION script, and the state both SIM clients must end in.
`RemoteChatResponse.response_actions[]` is how the brain DIRECTS the robot rather
than only speaking through it -- launch a module, leave one, sleep, arm the QR
scanner, run a named on-robot function, subscribe to perception events (see
DoD criterion 4 says the two SIM clients are interchangeable; on this channel that
was false until 2026-09-03: `sim/web/bridge.js::applyAction` acted on actions and
`script` is the four remote_chat responses `sim/test_bridge.mjs` already emits at the
browser SIM (event_id act-1 .. act-4), and `expected_state` is the state that file
already asserts the browser reached. So this golden is held from BOTH ends:
sim/tests/test_actions_reach_the_robot.py  the SIL robot reaches expected_state
sim/test_bridge.mjs                        the browser SIM reaches the same state
sim/tests/test_sim_client_parity.py        both clients name the same verbs and
so neither client can start disagreeing about what an action MEANT without a test
going red. Regenerate: drive VirtualMoxie._on_chat_reply over `script` and dump

script._why: a launch: the brain puts the child in an activity
an action-LESS entry carrying only an event subscription -- legal, not an error; the legacy singular mirrors it and must not fire twice
a verb this client does not implement, and a junk entry: both COUNTED and skipped, never raised -- a future server verb may not break an old client's turn
goodbye: leave the module and go to sleep, two actions on one response
